newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees end to garment row with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Manila sees end to garment row with U.S..

text.p: A top Philippine official said on Monday the country's dispute with the United States on rules of origin on textile exports was likely to be resolved soon.
"We hope to come up with an agreement before the end of the year," trade and industry secretary Cesar Bautista told reporters, but declined to give details.
In July, the U.S. imposed a rule under which garment exports would be credited to the country of origin.
Most of Manila's garment exports comprise of textiles from Hong Kong and China on which the final processing or finishing touches were done in the Philippines.
The rule meant that Philippine sales were considered Chinese exports and ran the risk of being barred once China'sexport quotas were completed.
The Philippines had earlier estimated that exports revenues would be cut by $30 million every year due to the new rule.
